item.title: Defending SaaS-based CRM platforms against OAuth abuse campaigns
item.description: Northwind describes an OAuth abuse campaign affecting SaaS CRM platforms.
item.content:encoded:
In a series of campaigns observed between mid-2025 and mid-2026, Northwind Security Research identified threat actor activity abusing trusted OAuth relationships between third-party applications and connected SaaS platforms, rather than relying on stolen credentials.

Northwind observed this activity across many tenants spanning multiple industries, including financial services, healthcare, retail, and manufacturing. Once an OAuth application was approved, the actor systematically queried and exfiltrated customer relationship management (CRM) records at scale, and in several cases established persistent access that survived password resets and routine remediation.

Northwind assesses this activity as a high-impact risk to affected organizations given the scale, persistence, and sensitivity of the exfiltrated data. These findings reinforce the importance of monitoring OAuth-connected applications, validating third-party integrations, and reviewing application permission configurations on an ongoing basis.

The following section describes the attack chain in additional technical detail, covering the initial access technique and the sequence of API calls used to enumerate available objects.

Session tokens issued to the malicious OAuth application were reused across subsequent requests, avoiding repeated re-authentication prompts that might draw administrator attention.

Defenders reviewing audit logs should expect a burst of read-heavy API activity shortly after a new OAuth application is granted consent, followed by large sequential export operations.
